approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored survivors. It keeps the highest-scoring survivors in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from several high-ranked score bands, and generates fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations with ordinary multistep continuation. Its direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange move is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws allocate evaluations among the pool members. Accepted offspring update both this model and the live breeding population, allowing repeated productive descendants to breed again.
approach.novelty: Remove only the unequal rank probabilities among parents that the existing breeding rule can already choose. For each request, keep exactly the original eligible support after partner exclusion and its existing fallback, then choose uniformly from that support. The earlier uniform-live sibling also made previously unsupported survivors eligible, so its score loss cannot distinguish support restriction from rank weighting. Frozen-parent and survivor-retention siblings changed other parts of the feedback loop; earlier core-balancing and success-credit experiments added different within-band preferences. This control supplies the missing weight-only contrast while recursive feedback, greedy retention and posterior allocation remain active. The preregistered prediction is that weaker preference for the highest supported ranks will reduce generating-parent quality and may lower final scores; either contribution sign or no material effect is informative.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent concentrates breeding probability within its already restricted live-parent support, leaving unresolved whether this extra rank concentration supports productive search or suppresses useful exploration among otherwise eligible survivors. Its current-profile baseline n-62daf219c70a is complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and seed population SD 0.02659287062806747. Its activation audit reports 629 strict best-parent beats among 4350 accepted offspring, 258 sequential incumbent gains and 2401 accepted offspring later reused as breeders; local wins and reuse therefore do not by themselves identify the value of rank weights. The direct same-Parent uniform-live control n-a56491c332aa changed both positive support and weights, admitted previously unsupported parents into 1427 evaluated products, and lowered mean final Top-1 by 0.04599801243765703. The fixed-initial-cohort control n-4d4b5eafa8b3 lowered the mean by 0.260205546950089 and supports preserving recursive reuse, not attributing either loss to weights alone. On their older binary-posterior Parent, n-69c038cb49ac core balancing and n-030a6ccbba7c historical-success weighting lowered means by 0.020256296737091634 and 0.02157946287432137 despite some improved local counts. These are warnings against treating more coverage or parent beats as stronger absolute offspring production; neither tests uniformity on the original support of the current count-posterior Parent. The limitation addressed here is this unresolved concentration-versus-quality tradeoff, not an established claim that uniformity improves search.
hypothesis: Remove nonuniform score-rank weighting conditional on the original same-state positive breeding support: choose uniformly from the increasing-rank union of the inherited positive-probability eligible quantile groups after original partner exclusion and empty-group fallback, retaining the original band-choice call as passive and the original member-choice call as the sole active parent allocation.

finding_summary.headline: Within-support rank weights contribute: uniform sampling lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.057003.
finding_summary.insights:
Nonuniform weighting has positive conditional value even when the set of eligible parents is held fixed. This separates the weight question from the earlier uniform-live control, which also admitted previously unsupported survivors. It does not identify support-only value or the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation, and the two shared-baseline controls cannot be subtracted into independent component effects.

The extra local wins used a weaker reference. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 936, and distinct offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,521. Yet mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.383214 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.321688; sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 238 and their average size also fell. Broader use therefore did not preserve absolute search quality. Founder ancestry, chemical core coverage and later use are distinct descriptions, and none establishes the causal route to the score loss.

The molecular assessment finds more generic core identities on four tasks but fewer on median similarity, alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine chemistry. Useful-looking structural variety still includes reactive local bonds, demanding bridges and unresolved stereochemistry, with conventional-bond and less-bridged counterexamples. The high-scoring Parent decoration-hopping arrangement was not recovered in the most affected seed. These observations narrow plausible explanations but do not show that a specific chemical defect caused the loss or that a universal chemical restriction would help. The registered weight-only question is answered for this composition, budget and three-seed panel; support-only effects, chemical mediation and broader foundation value remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The control preserved the exact original positive breeding support in all 108,254 parent requests. Every request offered a nonuniform-law comparison, and 103,018 actual parent identities differed from the inherited choice made from the same saved post-band random state. Mean selected topness was 0.756082 versus the original same-state expectation of 0.883924, and mean parent score was 0.348279 versus 0.373596. Changed choices reached 4,020 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,269 of those offspring later bred. Greedy recursion, complete accepted-score learning and all 435 full candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.538667, a paired change of -0.057003, beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.113955, -0.012930 and -0.044124. All five task means declined, but four of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved: zaleplon seed 0 (+0.031351), decoration hopping seed 1 (+0.003856), sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.008015) and median similarity seed 2 (+0.006814). The other eleven declined. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.019563. Every formal session completed with its full oracle budget and no fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic amides, aza-diones and aryl amines retain reactive bonds, difficult bridges and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-f30747ffdbf8 produces substituted indole/partly hydrogenated quinoline amides, linked aza-aromatic and lactone/dione systems, aryl-bearing saturated amines, polycyclic lactams with sulfones, and fluorinated nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks. Every supplied Child and published code-Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory was read: all five objectives and Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are covered on both sides. No supplied trajectory path is missing and no objective is omitted. context.comparison separately reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. These are complete chemistry comparisons under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation conditions; they do not establish activation, component contribution, chemical mediation or an independent replication. Each task has 900 Child trajectory records, including 870 accepted optimizer proposal instances. Initial molecules and repeated identities across seeds must not be counted as new chemistry. The digest final_molecules excerpt contains late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; the full trajectories supplied the seed-level comparisons below. The accepted trajectories do not expose invalid, duplicate-rejected or unscored proposal-pool structures. The digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9632, 0.977, 0.9816, 0.9862 and 0.9667 in fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9563, 0.9747, 0.9736, 0.9793 and 0.8517. These measure whether a SMILES contains the specified text feature, not perceived ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Charge- and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Neutral strings nevertheless contain many potentially basic aliphatic amines. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 descriptors were computed on one CPU from these accepted records: all 9,000 Child-plus-Parent records parse, but parsing is not a synthesis, geometry, stability or activity test. The 4,350 Child optimizer rows include 2,491 rows with RDKit-flagged unassigned tetrahedral centres, and none has assigned atom or bond stereochemistry. Small rings, bridges and sulfoxides therefore often lack a specified stereochemical identity. The Child/Parent nonempty generic Murcko-core counts, in fixed task order, are 134/123, 347/276, 268/258, 393/405 and 156/92. These deterministic topology descriptors show substantial generated structural variation, including a counterexample to any claim of uniformly increased coverage. They do not measure generating-parent ancestry, independent founder reachability, synthetic plausibility or useful pharmacophore coverage. Within-seed leading molecules often remain related even when atom substitutions and ring edits produce different core keys. Overall diversity is therefore moderate rather than globally collapsed; neither unique SMILES nor multiple ancestral paths would establish useful scaffold diversity. Familiar medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, acyl halides, peroxides, imines and difficult ring junctions, supporting questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall drug-likeness. There are important conventional-bond counterexamples, so this is not a claim that every molecule is implausible. The supplied scores only support local structural associations; no exact missing target pharmacophore is inferred. Descriptor definitions, source hashes and molecule-level provenance are recorded in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot2-molecular/chemistry_audit.json and molecule_descriptors.jsonl. The transferable gaps retain their recorded origin in n-c55c3d520a2c, their reproduction as reported by the indexed Parent n-62daf219c70a assessment, and their qualified re-observation in this Child.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer heavy-atom counts range from 1 to 46, with median 25; the median RDKit-perceived ring count is 3 and aromatic-ring count 3. The seed-0 best (evaluation 261) has 26 heavy atoms: an indole anilide with a fluoromethoxy group and an additional fused four-membered N-methyl ring bearing carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 1 (evaluation 250, 25 heavy atoms) uses a partly hydrogenated quinoline-like ring, a hydroxyl-bearing saturated centre, fluoromethyl substitution and a fluoropyridyl amide. Seed 2 (evaluation 271, 25 heavy atoms) retains a methoxy/dimethyl indole bearing N-Br and an N-amino aryl amide. The families are compact and aromatic, with recognizable carbonyl chemistry, but small-ring annulation and unusual nitrogen substitution weaken synthetic plausibility. Halogen-string incidence is 0.9195. N-halogen bonds are actually perceived in 42 of 870 Child optimizer rows versus 445 of 870 Parent rows, so this liability is far from universal and must not be inferred merely from total halogen incidence. The Parent best structures instead include an indole-associated cumulene in seed 0, an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide in seed 1, and an aryl vicinal diketone in seed 2; all retain aromatic/carbonyl organization but do not define one required substituent.
liabilities: The seed-2 leader combines an indole N-Br bond with an N-N-containing amide. These are distinct local reactivity concerns, not ordinary aryl C-Br substitution.

The seed-0 additional fused four-membered nitrogen ring and its substituted saturated centre need geometric and stereochemical assessment; valence-valid SMILES alone do not establish an accessible synthesis.
Late output still includes a small cyclic peroxide and isolated hydrocarbons with floor scores, demonstrating loss of useful chemical context in some accepted proposals.
missing_features: Stable alternative nitrogen environments that preserve the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not consistently represented among the very best examples. They are not absent from the generator: the seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules contain no N-halogen bond.
The substituted saturated centres of the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders have no stereochemical assignment, and the fused small-ring geometry has not been established.

The visible scores do not identify a uniquely missing pharmacophore or justify adding aromatic rings or heteroatoms indiscriminately; plausible alternative connectivities carrying the observed favorable organization remain a coverage question.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child best scores are 0.4254027310763201, 0.4163503402962837 and 0.42956033293511225 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. The seed-0 amide and its ketone-containing, methoxy-substituted relative at evaluation 271 both score 0.4254027310763201: a carbonyl-linked aromatic arrangement persists, but a unique amide identity is not required in that pair. Seed-1 fluoromethyl and chloromethyl relatives at evaluations 145 and 277 both score 0.4145039882261785. A seed-2 indene hydrazide lacking the leading indole N-Br bond scores 0.40709922777124763, although its core also changes. Methane at seed 0/evaluation 273 and the four-membered cyclic peroxide at seed 1/evaluation 300 each score 0.0. The visible reward concerns the combined compact aromatic/carbonyl environment rather than ring presence, nitrogen halogenation or halogen identity alone. Published Parent best scores are seed 0, evaluation 289: 0.39405142067435733, seed 1, evaluation 293: 0.47411701813450596, seed 2, evaluation 294: 0.438972502037081. These differently substituted molecules provide a conditional chemistry comparison, not a causal explanation of the panel scores.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer heavy-atom counts range from 1 to 109, with median 35; the median perceived ring count is 5 and aromatic-ring count 4. Seed 0 (evaluation 242, 39 heavy atoms) links an N-methyl fused dione to an aryl thio-lactone and imine-rich unsaturated substituents, including an unsaturated four-membered carbocycle. Seed 1 (evaluation 296, 36 heavy atoms) links condensed oxygen-containing lactone/aza-aromatic regions through NH and carries methoxy, methylamino, chloromethyl-containing alkyl and S-Cl substituents. Seed 2 (evaluation 284, 23 heavy atoms) is a much more compact amino-linked aza-aromatic assembly with carbon-bound halogens, an O-F bond and an N-Cl bond. Thus the output is neither uniformly oversized nor ring-poor. Synthetic plausibility is limited by local reactive groups, unsaturated small rings and elaborated fusion patterns. The Parent seed-0 best is a compact linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione system; its other seeds retain linked aza-carbonyl/nitrile and peroxide/nitrite-containing families. Child and Parent share broad heterocyclic character while accessing visibly different leading arrangements.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains S-Cl, while the seed-2 leader contains O-F and N-Cl. Their reactivity cannot be equated with ordinary carbon-bound fluorine or chlorine.

The seed-0 imine-rich unsaturated substituents and small-ring unsaturation require stability and geometry assessment; the long elaborated relatives also create unnecessary route complexity without demonstrated score benefit.
Large structures coexist with compact leaders and tiny floor-scoring reagents. Neither maximum size nor a high ring count certifies useful or accessible chemistry.
missing_features: Consistent access to compact, synthetically credible linked heterocyclic arrangements is unresolved. The Parent and Child show several arrangements, so the deficit is not an inability to build aromatic nitrogen rings.

Conventional peripheral replacements at comparable observed scores are incompletely explored, but near-leading examples without S-Cl or without both N-Cl and O-F are real counterexamples to a universal requirement for those bonds.
Geometry and stereochemical identity remain unestablished for the dense fused systems and substituted alkyl centres. The observations do not identify an exact absent target-specific substructure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused-dione molecule scores 0.548381482770623, whereas ClCl at seed 1/evaluation 285 gives the observed floor 0.5. Child seed best scores are 0.5977525513129228, 0.6286764705882353 and 0.6140166770661977. The seed-1 related lactone assembly at evaluation 205 lacks the S-Cl substituent and already scores 0.6264068304041692; this is a near-family comparison, not proof that adding S-Cl helps. The seed-2 late amino-linked aza-aromatic at evaluation 300 has neither N-Cl nor O-F and scores 0.6124979011585605, close to its seed leader despite other changes. The extensively elaborated seed-0 final molecule scores 0.5952300691050059, below the more compact best in that seed. Reward is associated with joined heteroaromatic/carbonyl regions; extra size, ring closures and reactive halogen bonds are not independently supported requirements. Published Parent best scores are seed 0, evaluation 281: 0.8561477222467935, seed 1, evaluation 296: 0.6248206599713055, seed 2, evaluation 296: 0.6178024026512013. In particular, the Parent seed-0 high-scoring linked aza-carbonyl/thione arrangement is not recovered among the Child seed-0 leaders, while the other Child seeds provide different chemical alternatives.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer heavy-atom counts range from 1 to 72, with median 33; median perceived ring count is 4 and aromatic-ring count 2. Seed 0 (evaluation 288, 32 heavy atoms) presents aliphatic and aryl amino groups on a polycycle containing a sulfoxide tether, methoxy, alkenyl and carbon-halogen substituents. Seed 1 (evaluation 231, 29 heavy atoms) combines a densely bridged/caged aliphatic diamine with a fluorinated biaryl region, benzylic chloride and N-hydroxymethyl substitution. Seed 2 (evaluation 291, 31 heavy atoms) instead has an azetidine, a secondary aminoalkyl linker and terminal imine between aromatic regions, one containing a thiol and a fused ether ring. Available aliphatic amines and aromatic surface are already present; neutral SMILES do not imply absent basic centres. Halogen-string incidence is 0.9908, mostly involving carbon-bound halogens. The Parent best examples span a flexible tertiary arylalkyl amine and substituted pyrrolidine families, demonstrating alternatives to the Child cage-like structures. These recognizable amine/aromatic motifs have plausible synthetic handles, but the dense junctions, benzylic halides, imines and unassigned stereochemistry keep overall plausibility conditional.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader has a benzylic chloride and N-hydroxymethyl substitution on a complex diamine framework; both local stability and bridge geometry need assessment.
The seed-2 leader combines an imine tail and aryl thiol with unspecified saturated centres. The seed-0 sulfoxide also introduces stereochemical possibilities beyond carbon centres.
Halogen-rich aromatic frameworks and dense saturated junctions can give high supplied scores without demonstrating solubility, a synthetic route, a realizable bound geometry or biological activity.
missing_features: The successful saturated amine/aromatic arrangements lack specified stereochemical identity. RDKit flags unassigned tetrahedral centres in 850 of the 870 optimizer rows here.

Consistently accessible alternatives preserving useful amine/aromatic spacing without dense cages or labile imine/benzylic-halide attachments are not established at every leading score. Conventional cyclic amines and the Parent flexible family are important existing counterexamples.
Neither additional amines nor formal positive charge can be named as the missing chemistry from this record: available amines are already common and protonation was not measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine thioester at seed 1/evaluation 17 scores 0.00016747245492913543, and a small methoxy/fluoro/chloro arene at seed 2/evaluation 166 scores 0.0022311965578061463. The amine-rich Child leaders score 0.9555154834481319, 0.9847597431011265 and 0.9475404637535233 across seeds. This associates higher supplied scores with available aliphatic amines placed within larger aromatic frameworks, rather than total nitrogen, sulfur or halogen count. A less densely bridged piperidine/aryl-ether relative at seed 1/evaluation 267 scores 0.9666683423709845, so the cage is not a universal high-score requirement. Seed-2 evaluation 264, with an unsaturated azetidine ring, scores 0.9434507702807099; saturating that ring in evaluation 291 gives 0.9475404637535233. Conversely, the multiply changed late seed-2 molecule at evaluation 298 still carries amines and halogens but scores only 0.06059234722733506. Their arrangement matters, and this multi-edit contrast does not identify a single detrimental group. Published Parent best scores are seed 0, evaluation 284: 0.9999989177995104, seed 1, evaluation 261: 0.9969753164881906, seed 2, evaluation 241: 0.9999934235240012, in flexible and conventional cyclic-amine families. These are oracle observations, not measured binding affinities or evidence of biological selectivity.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer heavy-atom counts range from 1 to 62, with median 33; median perceived ring count is 6 and aromatic-ring count 3. Seed 0 (evaluation 245, 36 heavy atoms) makes a propyl aza-arene/phenyl framework with an ethyl ester and tightly connected N-methyl carbonyl rings. Seed 1 (evaluation 285, 35 heavy atoms) combines a quinoline-like aromatic region with an ether-linked polycycle and a large amino/lactam ring; RDKit perceives a twelve-membered ring in this structure. Seed 2 (evaluation 287, 35 heavy atoms) favors an N-aryl condensed aromatic core annulated to an eight-membered nitrogen/lactam ring bearing a methylsulfone. These are substantial polycycles with carbonyl acceptors, tertiary or amide nitrogens, alkoxy groups and little halogen dependence: halogen-string incidence is 0.1678. The Parent also produces bridged lactams and quinoline-linked dicarbonyl amines, with median 30 heavy atoms and 5 perceived rings. The Child is more ring-rich in this descriptor reading, but its generic core count is 393 versus Parent 405, and the alternative leading seed-2 family prevents a claim of complete scaffold collapse. Recognizable functional groups coexist with demanding medium-ring connectivity, so synthetic plausibility remains questionable rather than absent.
liabilities: Dense bridges, fused unsaturation and medium or large nitrogen rings make synthetic routes and ring conformations nontrivial even at moderate atom counts.

The close seed-1 high-scoring relative contains an N-N connection. Such environments require individual assessment; the high-scoring seed-2 carbon-bound sulfone is a recognizable stable functional class and should not be conflated with reactive sulfur-halogen chemistry.
Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 658 of 870 optimizer rows, while explicit atom and bond stereochemistry remains absent.
missing_features: The leading polycycles do not establish simpler, synthetically accessible connectivities that preserve the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement at the same observed scores.
Stereochemical and conformational identity is unresolved at the saturated bridges and in the medium or large rings; perceived ring counts alone supply neither.

Plausible independent alternatives within each leading seed family remain limited, but actual alternative families and many core topologies are present. No exact missing objective-specific motif can be inferred from these score plateaus.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329 and acetylene at seed 1/evaluation 173 scores 0.0. Child seed best scores are 0.20599226856861022, 0.21487303262816246 and 0.23281726848556925. Seed-0 evaluation 215, the related carbon-containing aromatic ring in place of its aza analogue, scores 0.20514055865616304, close to 0.20599226856861022; the seed-1 N-N-containing ring relative at evaluation 232 scores 0.21269248984883138, close to its N-C-N-containing leader. In seed 2, the ethoxy/methyl aryl lactam-sulfone at evaluation 232 scores 0.2299139228044128; replacing the aryl methyl by ethyl at evaluation 287 gives 0.23281726848556925. These comparisons associate reward with the whole aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization and show modest sensitivity to several local changes; they do not identify one absent heteroatom or justify greater ring complexity. Published Parent best scores are seed 0, evaluation 293: 0.2258403994203931, seed 1, evaluation 278: 0.2214095461892601, seed 2, evaluation 261: 0.22600312875247064. Different seed outcomes and frameworks must be retained rather than reduced to a claim that more rings or more core identities are uniformly useful.

per_task.generated_character: Optimizer heavy-atom counts range from 1 to 61, with median 28; median perceived ring count is 4 and aromatic-ring count 3. Seed 0 (evaluation 211, 26 heavy atoms) joins an N-methyl dione/four-membered nitrogen-ring system to cyclopropyl and fluorinated phenol/acyl-fluoride substituents. Seed 1 (evaluation 300, 27 heavy atoms) retains a fused nitrogen-rich dione bearing N-F, cyclobutyl and fluorinated unsaturated carbocycle/acyl-fluoride regions. Seed 2 (evaluation 293, 28 heavy atoms) uses an extended fused aza-aromatic dione with N-F joined to an unsaturated, bridged amine/thioether ring system. These are compact polar polycycles rather than simple fluorinated chains; the larger aromatic labels and bridges do not establish a credible geometry. Halogen-string incidence is 0.8379 and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence 0.0345. Perceived N-halogen incidence is 263 of 870 Child optimizer rows versus 476 of 870 Parent rows. The seed-0 Child best has no N-F, while the seed-2 best has no acyl fluoride: neither liability is universal. The Parent seed-0 and seed-1 leaders are related fluorinated imino/dione families, while its seed-2 leader combines a large nitrogen ring with a small cyclic cumulene. The Child highest examples do not require that cyclic cumulene, but still retain different local reactivity and geometry concerns.
liabilities: Acyl fluoride is an acylating functional group, chemically distinct from ordinary aryl C-F; it is retained in the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders. Other leading molecules carry N-F bonds.
Unsaturated small nitrogen rings and bridged amine/thioether systems create geometry and route concerns; nearby accepted relatives include cyclic cumulated double bonds.
A strong local score change can leave a questionable framework intact. RDKit parseability and high supplied scores do not establish stability or makeability of the resulting structure.
missing_features: Consistently conventional local bond environments that retain the favorable compact nitrogen/carbonyl/carbocycle organization are not established among all leaders; the separate no-N-F and no-acyl-fluoride examples are important partial counterexamples.

Geometrically credible alternatives to small-ring unsaturation, extended aromatic-labelled rings and dense bridges are not demonstrated at each leading score. Noncumulated high-scoring molecules show that cyclic cumulenes are not required.

Saturated ring centres lack explicit stereochemistry, and tautomeric/conformational identity has not been established. More fluorine, aromaticity or ring count cannot be inferred as the missing answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed best scores are 0.37262308478678474, 0.4950209187717372 and 0.5591001407480495. The seed-1 final two records are especially informative: evaluation 299 with core-bound F scores 0.003243755069926903, while replacing that substituent by cyclobutyl at evaluation 300 gives 0.4950209187717372 with the remaining cited framework retained. This supports the importance of attached carbocyclic context within that scaffold, not a general instruction to fluorinate. Within the seed-2 bridged family, changing the N-methyl of evaluation 281 to N-ethyl at evaluation 300 changes 0.5095677113917223 to 0.20922546931191585; elaboration is not uniformly rewarded. The much larger fused-dione assembly at seed 2/evaluation 26 scores 2.3244240434690467e-61, and isolated F at seed 1/evaluation 277 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. A seed-1 cyclic-cumulene relative at evaluation 268 scores 0.45821707742094264, below its noncumulated seed leader, although other features differ too. Published Parent best scores are seed 0, evaluation 276: 0.6510211907030741, seed 1, evaluation 290: 0.4870057305679067, seed 2, evaluation 273: 0.7208853668418119. The visible association is a specific compact nitrogen/carbonyl/carbocycle balance; none of these contrasts certifies acyl-fluoride or N-F stability, identifies a unique missing pharmacophore, or attributes the scores to one generator component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reported as reproduced by code-Parent n-62daf219c70a, and is qualitatively re-observed in n-f30747ffdbf8 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation-per-objective profile. Current leaders include N-Br, N-F, N-Cl, O-F, S-Cl, acyl fluoride, benzylic chloride or imine environments; the original source and Parent also documented reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide chemistry. Counterexamples matter: high-scoring compact amides and aryl amines without N-halogen bonds occur, a near-leading aza-aromatic lacks both N-Cl and O-F, and a related lactone assembly lacks S-Cl. The missing capability is consistency and environment awareness, not inability to produce conventional bonds or basic nitrogen.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional local bond environments when varying useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations should distinguish carbon-bound aromatic halogens and conventional sulfones from reactive heteroatom-halogen, acyl-halide and other labile local environments, while supplying plausible alternatives that preserve useful arrangements learned from accepted task-local feedback. This is a conditional chemistry association, not attribution to the changed component or evidence that a universal chemical filter improves the benchmark.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reported as reproduced by code-Parent n-62daf219c70a, and is qualitatively re-observed in n-f30747ffdbf8 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation-per-objective profile. The original source and Parent include small cyclic cumulenes and demanding nitrogen-ring geometries. The current molecules add fused four-membered nitrogen rings, an unsaturated four-membered carbocycle, dense diamine cages and medium or large lactam rings. The accepted structures parse, but no conformational or route evidence was supplied. Conventional cyclic amines, less bridged high-scoring analogues and noncumulated fluorinated leaders are counterexamples to any claim that complex bridges or cumulated bonds are required.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can produce ring graphs without consistently establishing credible geometry, unsaturation or manageable bridge connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring edits need sensitivity to ring size, unsaturation geometry and bridge connectivity, with feasible alternative topologies that preserve learned functional-group relationships. Ordinary small rings and useful fused systems should remain distinguishable from unsupported geometry. This inherited and current output association supplies no component-specific cause and no demonstrated score benefit from a geometric restriction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reported as reproduced by code-Parent n-62daf219c70a, and is qualitatively re-observed in n-f30747ffdbf8 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation-per-objective profile. The digest stereocentre-string incidence remains 0.0 on every supplied objective. Read-only perception flags unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,491 of 4,350 current accepted optimizer rows, and none of those output rows has assigned atom or bond stereochemistry. Neutral strings nevertheless contain available aliphatic amines, so charge absence is not an amine-coverage deficit. Achiral molecules are also present; absence of stereochemical notation is only a missing identity where a stable stereochemical distinction exists.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves stereochemical identity unresolved after generating potentially stereogenic saturated centres, sulfur centres and bridges.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and graph transformations should preserve or deliberately resolve relevant stereochemistry and distinguish configurationally stable centres from achiral or rapidly interconverting cases. Protonation and tautomerism need separate treatment rather than inference from neutral SMILES. These observations establish unresolved identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or attribution to the intervention.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reported as reproduced by code-Parent n-62daf219c70a, and is qualitatively re-observed in n-f30747ffdbf8 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation-per-objective profile. The original source and Parent showed tiny floor-scoring products and unnecessarily elaborate relatives. Current accepted rows again include isolated halogens, hydrocarbons and a cyclic peroxide at observed floors, as well as a very large fused-dione assembly with an extremely small supplied score. In close current relatives, replacing a substantial carbocyclic substituent by fluorine loses much of the observed score, while extending an N-methyl to N-ethyl also lowers it. Compact high-scoring heterocycles and a less bridged high-scoring cyclic amine are counterexamples to treating small size or simplification itself as undesirable.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional-group context while controlling destructive fragmentation and redundant elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local accepted feedback to preserve informative molecular context while allowing selective simplification or replacement of dispensable regions. Neither a fixed minimum size nor a blanket preference for larger molecules follows from these condition-dependent examples. The chemistry describes an inherited output limitation and does not establish that a particular allocation or retention component caused it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c, reported as reproduced by code-Parent n-62daf219c70a, and is qualitatively re-observed in n-f30747ffdbf8 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied batch-size-10, 300-evaluation-per-objective profile. Current leading excerpts repeatedly vary substituents or ring segments within retained aromatic amide, aza-dione, aryl-amine and lactam families, as in the source and Parent. This is qualified by real between-seed family differences and many perceived core topologies. One current leading aza-aromatic group has a single generic core among its highest ten accepted molecules, whereas a current high-scoring amine group spans eight generic cores among ten. Typed core changes can follow local atom substitutions, while generic core changes can follow local bridges; neither by itself establishes chemical independence, makeability or useful coverage. No founder-ancestry measurement is inferred from the trajectories or these scaffold descriptors.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent, plausible alternatives to the leading family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore chemically feasible scaffold reorganizations that retain useful functional-group relationships learned from feedback, and assess whether the alternatives remain useful as accepted descendants. Keep canonical identity, typed core, generic topology and generating-parent ancestry as distinct evidence. This conditional coverage gap is not global collapse, a component attribution, or evidence that uniformly increasing diversity improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
